claims.text: The starting additively manufactured Al0.2Co1.5CrFeNi1.5Ti0.3 alloy has a single-phase, chemically homogeneous fcc matrix.
The starting alloy has high strength and fatigue performance.
High-temperature degradation is primarily governed by the kinetics and chemistry of thin protective oxide scales on the fcc matrix.
Cr and Ti selectively oxidize in Al0.2Co1.5CrFeNi1.5Ti0.3.
Selective oxidation of Cr and Ti produces a mixed oxide layer.
The composition, adhesion, and continuity of the mixed oxide layer depend on the ambient gas.
Under oxidizing conditions, a relatively stable protective oxide scale forms and limits further degradation.
Under reducing conditions, the protective scale is destabilized or forms insufficiently.
Failure to form a protective scale under reducing conditions accelerates internal elemental diffusion and phase destabilization.
During oxidizing exposure, Cr and Ti diffuse to the alloy surface.
Cr and Ti form an adherent, dual-phase mixed oxide containing Cr2O3 and TiO2 components.
The Cr2O3- and TiO2-containing layer temporarily passivates the alloy and slows degradation.
Reducing exposure produces a thinner or less coherent oxide layer than oxidizing exposure.
Samples exposed to reducing atmospheres will lose mechanical properties faster than samples exposed to oxidizing atmospheres.
Prolonged oxidizing exposure may cause oxide-scale cracking and localized failure.
Overall degradation will remain less severe under oxidizing conditions than under reducing conditions.
The as-printed baseline has minimal surface oxide formation.
